ftbquests.chapter.renewability_and_you.q: Granite Dust centrifuges into Redrock Dust and the familiar Silicon Dioxide Dust.
Silicon Dioxide is generally just great to have, and Redrock centrifuges into Calcite (that's renewable Calcium) and Flint.
Redrock, Silicon Dioxide...
Yet another &bForge Hammer&r step, but you'll be making &dSand&r renewably. With renewable Sand comes renewable Glass (remember to try using an &9Arc Furnace&r for that sweet &adoubled&r yield!).
Quartz Sand Dust centrifuges into a chanced output of &3Certus Quartz&r Dust.
Two vast and trunkless legs of stone...
Basalt Dust centrifuges into Olivine, a material which can be used to substitute Emerald in a small handful of recipes - for example, when making Engraved Crystal Chips.
You also get a pittance of Dark Ash.
Olivine, Dark Ashes...
This was touched upon in the &5EV&r chapter, but we'll focus on what this distillation gets you here.

The Nitrogen output is &bsubstantial&r, and can help you keep any &ePyrolyse Ovens&r running. You should buffer some of the Nitrogen so you can &aboost your EBFs&r - faster recipe times save your sanity and energy in equal measures.
{@pagebreak}
Helium and Argon yields are low, but ideally you can run the Air Distillation as a &dpassive process&r every so often to keep your supplies topped up. Both are used to &aboost EBF speeds&r.
&bCrushed Ice&r is... well, &bCrushed Ice&r. Maybe you could open a cocktail bar?
Nitrogen, Helium, Argon....
I promise I won't sell my air as a commodity!
Liquid Air
By collecting Air with a &6Gas Collector&r and cooling it to Liquid state with a &3Vacuum Freezer&r, you can then distill the liquid Air for a plethora of valuable resources.

You thought that was all? Air collection isn't limited to the &2Overworld&r - whilst you'll require a higher-tier Distillation Tower to distill the "higher" tiers of liquid Air, you can also process air from the &4Nether&r and the &5End&r. This process is mostly optional, but you'll definitely find it to be a rewarding one.
Things are up in the air right now...
Air truly is wonderful.
All Kinds Of Air (Distillation)
Carbon Monoxide is useful when making &6Butyraldehyde&r for your Laminated Glass in &9late IV&r.
&6Coal Gas&r can be processed in a Distillation Tower for a variety of useful outputs.
Helium-3 is only used in &bFusion&r, and Neon is used to boost a single &aBlast Furnace&r recipe - &4UHV&r superconductors!
Ashes are always useful for the handful of resources they grant.
Carbon, Coal Gas, Helium-3...
It's not all hellish in the Nether.
Liquid Nether Air
Deepslate centrifuges into... you guessed it... Silicon Dioxide! You may want to set this up for the guaranteed Biotite output, as Biotite electrolyses into Fluorine.
This is obviously a far better source of Biotite than Stone Dust. Hopefully, you didn't waste your time setting that up!
Silicon Dioxide, Fluorine...
Andesite Dust will get you some delicious Asbestos Dust, and some Saltpeter Dust to boot.
Asbestos is a slow source of Magnesium, and Saltpeter has a variety of uses in chemistry.
Asbestos, Saltpeter... (No Create)
Calcite, Magnesium...
Pulverise your Diorite into Dust, then centrifuge for Mirabilite Dust and Clay Dust.
Mirabilite yields minimal Sulfur, but Clay Dust is the real treasure here. When electrolysed, you'll get some Aluminium for your troubles. Not bad!
Mirabilite, Clay...
Yup - &brenewable&r Glass.
Glass'll always be useful throughout your playthrough in a variety of recipes.
Glass Hurts, doesn't it...

You may be wondering how to obtain &6large quantities&r of common resources used in &bGregTech&r. This might be old news to seasoned players, but it's actually possible to set up &dpassive processes&r to make various materials and chemicals &2fully renewable&r.
We've added this chapter to lead you towards some setups that you &7&omight&r desire. Obviously, there's no need to do all of these, but who doesn't love &2"free" resources&r.

&9&lA footnote:&r There's no way we could document all of the renewable routes in &bGregTech&r. This quest page merely serves as a primer to lead &6newer players&r through their options. Not every option listed in this quest book is optimal, so we urge you to experiment!
Very conscious of you!
I love renewable resources!
Promoting a Sustainable Playthrough
Just Forge Hammer that Cobblestone and you'll get some &dGravel&r.
Gravel macerates into &6Stone Dust&r, but with a low chance of Flint when the recipe is performed in a &6HV Macerator&r or above. You probably want to sift for Flint, anyway!
Flint Dust centrifuges into &aSilicon Dioxide&r, which is then electrolysed for Silicon and Oxygen.
cp_gravelpit
Oh, we're only just getting started.
Cobblestone
The Joy of Cobblestone
Ah, the Rock Crusher - such an unassuming machine that initially appears to only really be a builder's best friend. Who could look past infinite Cobblestone, Deepslate, or Obsidian?

Don't be fooled, though, as this little machine might just shock you with the array of materials it makes renewable when you macerate its rocks down to dust form. The surrounding quests will clue you in.
More like game breaking, am I right?
Rock Breaking
&6Stone Dust&r can be centrifuged in &bMV&r for a wide range of miscellaneous materials. It's a slow and expensive process, but you may wish to check it out.
Obviously, Quartzite is Quartzite. Did you know that you could extract any excess Quartzite into &eLiquid Glass&r?
&aPotassium Feldspar&r electrolyses into some incredibly useful resources.
You also have a (low) chance for &dBiotite&r, which notably electrolyses for a very slow source of &bFluorine&r.
Finally, &aMetal Mixture dust&r is useless until you can centrifuge it at &5EV&r. Pretty much all of its outputs when centrifuged are very useful.
Small Stone, Big Byproducts
By placing some Redstone Dust into your Rock Breaker, you'll find yourself making some Obsidian.
Obsidian Dust is quite useful, as it electrolyses into Iron.
Fallout: New Vegas, Iron...

&5Ender Air&r is probably the most interesting of the three airs to distill. Requiring an &9IV Distillation Tower&r and distilling in batches of 200,000L, you'll need to outfit your DT with at least an &9IV&r Input Hatch (or an &5ME Hatch&r if you're inclined).

You're getting a ton of Nitrogen, Oxygen, Helium, and Deuterium - the latter of which is commonly used in &aFusion&r. Tritium is used to make &6Helium Plasma&r, which is commonly agreed to be the best plasma for &2power generation&r.
{@pagebreak}

Krypton and Xenon are your run-of-the-mill &aEBF-boosting&r Noble gases. At this point, you should consider running most (if not all) of your EBF recipes on &bCircuit 2&r to benefit from the faster durations.
Would you look at that - you get &dRadon&r as well! It's a slow process, especially when you consider that your old setup (did you set it up?) already loops on itself, but &dmore Radon&r is nice.

Last but not least, you're getting a low chance of &3Ender Pearl Dust&r. The chances are low enough that you shouldn't give up on the Mixer recipe just yet... but once again, more &3Ender Pearls&r are nice!
Nitrogen, Oxygen, Helium, Krypton, Xenon, Radon, Ender Pearls...
I'm surprised I can breathe in the End.
Liquid Ender Air
Not to be confused with regular Granite, Red Granite has some useful utility when the dust is processed.
Electrolysing it yields Aluminium for slightly fewer steps than the renewable Clay electrolysis.
Aluminium...

Just so you're aware - vanilla farms such as &7Iron Golems&r or &ePiglins&r have been &4disabled&r in this pack. There are obviously ways to cheese the pack (such as some good old Minecraft &acapitalism&r, &mif you catch our drift&r), but we encourage you to try to play without taking advantage of some notorious vanilla "&ocheese&r".

It's possible that in the future, we'll just make a core-mod for the pack, so players can re-enable the disabled mob drops. For now, the drops are disabled via &5KubeJS script&r, so if you're script-savvy, the file can be removed at &o&7server_scripts/vanilla/loot_drops.js&r.
Is it safe? Is it alright?
Oh, darn. That kinda sucks.
What about my mob farm?
ftbquests.chapter.steam_age.quest03DBF19: &dSteam Machines&r accept any Steam that is pumped from nearby Boilers into their internal storage tank. They will run recipes from EMI up to 32 EU/t (&7LV&r-tier).
&6This quest unlocks a new tutorial on Steam in the &lTips and Tricks&r&6 tab - check it out to learn more!&r
ftbquests.chapter.steam_age.quest0C30101: Now that you have Steel, you can make a Hang Glider. This might be a good item to grab before you hit up the &cNether&r.
If you don't have enough Leather yet, make a &9Butchering Knife&r and employ its inherent Looting III to hunt some cows.
&l&3Lore:&r&o The Hang Glider originally came from a mod known as OpenBlocks. As its utility was too great to be left on earlier versions, it was ported all the way up to modern versions.
No, it's Steve with a glider!
Is it a Phantom? Is it an Elytra?
ftbquests.chapter.steam_age.quest13901DA: The &bPrimitive Water Pump&r is an easy way to automatically generate water for your boilers. It doesn't physically pump water from the world, instead generating it &einternally&r. Therefore, you don't need access to a &3body of water&r to make use of it. However, the humidity of the biome does apply a negligible bonus to its water production.

It's a multiblock, so &5consult EMI&r for the structure. Multiblocks can be previewed in-world if you sneak right-click the "&a&ocontroller&r" block with an empty hand (in this case, the controller block is the &bPrimitive Water Pump&r itself).
&6Small tip for you:&r no need to worry about your base's biome for now, as your boilers will need very little water to keep up.

The &cOutput Hatch&r is where water will be generated. You can make it face up or down to auto-output water into your pipes, which can go &ethrough&r the Treated Wood Frames - just place the pipe before you encase it in the frames.
Later you can use a &8ULV&r or &7LV&r Output Hatch to further boost the Pump's output.
&2Reminder:&r Use a Wrench to rotate GregTech blocks (sneak right-click).
&l&3Lore:&r&o This Multiblock was ported from GT IMPACT, a classic 1.7.10 GregTech modpack.
There's no such thing as "free" water
ftbquests.chapter.steam_age.quest1436DB8: Not many items are made in the &3Extractor&r during the &6Steam Age&r, but it's used to make &9Rubber&r, which you'll need after Steel.
You can also process Dirt in the Extractor for &aBones&r, which makes getting &aBone Meal&r a lot easier for Peaceful players.
ftbquests.chapter.steam_age.quest15923B4: You DO have access to some beefy &bfluid storage&r right now, but you'll need to make a &eMultiblock&r to access it!
This Quest generously rewards an extra &6Coke Oven&r. Make the most of GTCEu's &bwallsharing&r mechanic, and place it next to an existing Coke Oven to save on casings.
&l&3Lore:&r&o Just like Drums, these multiblocks are ported from GregTech 6.
The &3Wooden Multiblock Tank&r&r holds &a250,000 mB&r, but you won't be able to use it to store &chot Fluids&r such as Lava, or &cGases&r such as Steam or Oxygen.
The &3Bronze Multiblock Tank&r holds &a500,000 mB&r, lifiting the maximum fluid tempreture and can now store &cGases&r.
The &3Steel Multiblock Tank&r holds &a1,000,000 mB&r, and lifts all the aforementioned fluid restrictions.
Get &eany&r of the Tanks to complete this quest. The Steel version is &dway too expensive&r right now - so you should probably make the Wooden  or Bronze one instead.
Fluid transfer can either be facilitated through the Controller block, or through up to &atwo Valves&r.
Valves can &9auto-output&r by placing them on the &dbottom layer&r and making them &dface down&r (as always, use a &5Wrench&r to adjust their facing).
Unlike &3Drums&r, these Tanks aren't portable... but you probably guessed that already.
So long, and Tanks for all the fish!
ftbquests.chapter.steam_age.quest1931FC6: With the creation of this machine, many recipes that once required you to use a hammer can instead be made here!
It can process &bCobblestone into Gravel&r, and &dGravel into Sand&r - and it's zippy at that to boot.
Last but not least, it makes &aPlates&r at a better ratio: &6three Ingots for two Plates&r. A worthwhile investment!
You know what? &aBonus&r! We'll give you the &8Anvil&r back if you craft the Forge Hammer. This is a gentle reminder that you can repair GregTech tools in an Anvil.
ftbquests.chapter.steam_age.quest1C50A75: The &bMacerator&r frees you from the painful process of &egrinding stuff into dust&r with a &3Mortar&r, but at the steep cost of time. Processing a single piece of Iron Ore in this machine will take &ctwenty seconds&r - twice the time it takes to smelt an ingot in a furnace!
The Macerator also marks the advent of &eOre Processing&r, but that's a scary topic that we'll dip our toes into in the next quest.
The macerator will output only the first item shown in recipes from EMI. The other slots are locked until you make a &6HV&r Macerator. How unfortunate...
Our (&oimportant!&r) advice: it's actually better to keep directly smelting for now! The efficiency loss is made up with faster mining. Use the Macerator to make things like &aClay Dust&r instead!
ftbquests.chapter.steam_age.quest1FFD224: &bFluid Pipes&r will transport &7Steam&r between machines for you.

Each Pipe has a certain throughput in mB/t, and a &6Temperature Limit&r. This is relevant right now, as Steam will burn Wooden Pipes. Some pipes have &bspecial&r attributes you don't need to worry about for now.

Each material has several sizes for Pipes. The bigger the Pipe, the &ahigher&r the throughput, but the more &dexpensive&r the craft. For example, a normal &6Bronze Fluid Pipe&r transfers 120 mB/t. (It also has a 1,200 mB internal buffer!)
Get any &6Bronze Fluid Pipe&r to complete this quest. The &6small&r and &enormal&r ones in particular are used in other recipes as well.
&aReminder:&r 1 second = 20 ticks... assuming the server isn't lagging.
&dNote:&r GT6-style Pipes are enabled. It means that placing Pipes connects them only to the block they were placed against. To open more connections, use your Wrench on the pipe.
You can also shift-right click with your Wrench to disable input from a side. This can help counteract sloshing &7(liquids travelling in an undesired direction)&r.
ftbquests.chapter.steam_age.quest2299753: Make the listed molds for future alloy smelting. Be sure to make &aMolds&r - don't make &cExtruder Shapes&r, as they're used in a different machine.
The reward for this quest will alleviate &da lot of pain&r when it comes to crafting &bGears&r.
Reduce the amount of malding by molding
ftbquests.chapter.steam_age.quest236C886: If Lava is "too hot to handle", we've included a &6direct crafting recipe&r for &aPotions of Fire Resistance&r. EMI might look a little confusing, but don't worry - you can use &bWater Bottles&r in the potion recipe.

&l&3Lore:&r&o With the existence of &6Small Sulfur Ores&f scattered in GregTech 5 ore veins, you could mine enough Sulfur in the Overworld to skip having to visit the Nether. Sounds broken, but it was still as much of a grind as Nether travel!
A little bit of exploring never hurt anyone
ftbquests.chapter.steam_age.quest2493745: Use Mortars or a Macerator (your choice) to microcraft your way to Glass Dust, which you can then turn into a &aGlass Block&r.

If you are lost, a more detailed guide for this process is on the next page, but &dwe urge you to nose around EMI&r and figure out the recipe on your own. Being able to navigate EMI and parse recipes is an &6essential skill&r for completing this pack.
Glass will be easier later on. You've probably already noticed that juicy &3Arc Furnace&r recipe - don't worry, we'll get there soon.
Glass tubes will be required for your first Electronic Circuit.
First, use a &3method of pulverisation&r to turn Sand into &9Quartz Sand Dust&r.
Next, crush down some Flint into &9Flint Dust&r, and split this dust into tiny piles in a crafting grid.
Combine the two into &9Glass Dust&r, which can be molded into Glass in an Alloy Smelter with a &9Block Mold&r.
ftbquests.chapter.steam_age.quest2724086: Ever wanted your pipes to look &leven&r cooler? Now you can!
Fluid and Item Pipes can be placed inside of Frameboxes, giving your base an &6unparalleled level of beauty&r!
All you - dear player - need to do is right-click a frame onto a pipe &7(or a pipe onto a frame)&r, and you're done.
Spaghetti has never looked so swanky!
ftbquests.chapter.steam_age.quest2B74E56: &6GregTech&r can quickly get &4overwhelming&r with the plethora of fluids it introduces, so you may be looking for a way to store them.
Introducing... &aDrums&r! They have large internal buffers, and any &aDrum&r can be broken and picked up and will &dkeep the fluid&r inside.

Additionally, &binternal tanks&r from machines will interact with items containing fluid. This is great for manual crafting - this means you can use fluid drums instead of multiple buckets in crafting. To &5void fluid&r contained in a Drum, place it alone in any crafting grid.

Multiblock I/O
Transporting EU is done via direct connection, using &aWires&r or &aCables&r.
{@pagebreak}
GT6-style Cables are &denabled&r. It means that placing Cables will only connect them to the block they were placed against. To open more connections, use your &5Wire Cutter&r on the grid.
{@pagebreak}

&2GTCEu&r Cables now have &6native RF support&r! You can plug any RF appliance into an EU source and it will automatically convert. The ratio is &a4 : 1&r (RF : EU). Not that you can produce RF in this pack - but it's a thought if you wanted to make your own!

Wires are the inferior option as they will &celectrocute&r you and &close more energy&r as the electricity travels through the wire, so you want to use insulated Cables. Keep in mind that you can't combine cables into thicker variants, so make sure you insulate the right thickness to avoid any headaches.

&cCable loss&r means you will have to stick your Machines close to your Generators, but that will only be a problem in earlygame. If you peek through the quest book, you will eventually be able to obtain &6Superconductors&r, sidestepping this issue!
{@pagebreak}
Keep in mind that GregTech cables suffer from "cable loss". Every block of cable that an EU packet travels will decrease its stored EU.

For instance, transferring &7LV&r current along 6 cables each with a loss of 5 EU/t will result in the packets arriving at their destination with a meagre 2 EU/t (32 - [6*5]). For this reason, you will want to keep your cables short until you can start to consider better alternatives.
{@pagebreak}

&6Superconductors&r are special Wires available for each Voltage tier. They don't have any Cable counterpart, but that isn't necessary, as they have absolutely &6zero cable loss&r! They also don't damage you when you touch them.
They are the best choice for wiring at any tier, if not a little expensive in comparison to the other wires.
Cables
&aRotors&r have a &9Power&r, &dEfficiency&r and &4Durability&r that are based on tool stats.
&9-&r The &aRotor&r can give a huge boost to &dFuel efficiency&r and &9Power&r production.
&9-&r You get a lot of satisfaction for setting them up properly (yay!)
{@pagebreak}
&l...and some cons of Large Turbines:
&9-&r Turbines work off &eInertia&r, which requires them to continuously run to achieve maximum Power.
&9-&r Any excess Energy produced will be &cvoided&r. You will &lneed&r to use large Energy Buffers and an &3Advanced Energy Detector&r if you wish to stay efficient.
&9-&r They require a &aRotor&r, which will lose durability over time and eventually &cbreak&r.
&9-&r A little bit of Math is required to get the expected results.
{@pagebreak}
A Turbine's &9Power&r output affects both the fuel consumption and the EU/t generation. It is calculated with the following formula:
&9Power&r is a multiplier applied to the production of the &3Turbine&r. This stacks multiplicatively with the &3Rotor Holder&r.
&eproduction = baseEUt x rotorPower x 2^(rotorHolderTier - turbineTier)&r
The &dEfficiency&r reduces fuel consumption, but does not alter the EU/t generation. It is calculated with the following formula:
&eefficiency = rotorEfficiency x (1 + 0.1 x (rotorHolderTier - turbineTier))&r
{@pagebreak}
Let's simulate a Large Steam Turbine, with an Ultimet Rotor and an &5EV&r Rotor Holder:
Production = 1024 x 1.60 x 2 = 3276 EU/t
Efficiency = 1.30 x 1.10 = 143%
(Therefore, steam consumption would be 4582 L/t - this is above a Titanium Boiler, or a Tungstensteel Boiler with ~70% throttle)
{@pagebreak}
Next, we'll analyse the Gas Turbine, with a Chrome Rotor and an &5EV&r Rotor Holder:
&dEfficiency&r reduces its fuel consumption. This again stacks multiplicatively with the &3Rotor Holder&r.
Production = 4096 x 1.70 x 1 = 5325 EU/t
Efficiency = 1.55 x 1.00 = 155%
(The same fuel consumption would produce 3435 EU/t using 6.7 Turbo Gas Turbines!)
{@pagebreak}
Finally, how about we check out the Plasma Turbine, with a HSS-S Rotor and a &cZPM&r Rotor Holder:
Production = 16834 x 2.50 x 4 = 168340 EU/t
Efficiency = 1.80 x 1.20 = 216%
(This is more than a ZPM Amp!)
&4Durability&r is the lifetime of the &aRotor&r in seconds, when the &3Turbine&r&r is active.
{@pagebreak}
&3Rotor Holders&r above the tier of the &3Large Turbine&r will multiplicatively &6double&r the production for every tier, whilst additively increasing the efficiency by 10% every tier.
{@pagebreak}
&lSome pros of Large Turbines:
&9-&r Turbines can scale &9Power&r production far, far higher than their base output, thanks to tiered &3Rotor Holders&r.
Large Turbine Mechanics
There are two really important factors to know when building Multiblocks.

Taking the EBF as an example, any tier of Energy/Bus/Hatch can be used, and they can be placed anywhere in place of a casing. Fluid Hatches are also optional, though you probably want them if you need to handle recipes involving fluid.
Check EMI, and remember to keep things versatile.
{@pagebreak}
Rule number one - check EMI!

This one was probably obvious, but EMI is so much more than just a cute picture of how the Multiblock looks when built! Use your mouse to &drotate&r the preview, and &9hover over the blocks used&r to view any extra information.
The EMI page also contains an ingredient list of required blocks. You can also &dright-click&r a block in the preview to get a display of all blocks that work in that specific position.
{@pagebreak}
Rule number two - multiblocks are versatile!

There is no "definite" way to form the Multiblock. Most of the time, you have complete freedom over the &9tier of Buses/Hatches&r used - and you also have the ability to&d choose where you want your inputs/outputs&r.
Multiblock University
Forming Multiblocks
&lWhy process ore?
{@pagebreak}
A pickaxe or mining hammer enchanted with Hammering, or a GregTech Hammer directly, gives Crushed Ores from breaking Ore blocks, but only at a 1:1 ratio.
Silk Touch is essential to obtain an ore block - this pack includes a recipe for the book.
{@pagebreak}
The rule bends for ores giving more than two dusts (such as &cRedstone&r), and for dusts that cannot be smelted (&cRedstone&r... again!).
However, you can still smelt the ore directly to get &9half the amount&r you would from the full processing.
{@pagebreak}
&dEMI does not indicate Impure Dust to Clean Dust conversion&r, so keep that in mind that you can &athrow them into filled cauldrons&r.
{@pagebreak}
Take this reward for listening to us waffle on WITHOUT nodding off!
The main purpose of GregTech Ore Processing is to provide &abyproducts&r on top of the initial outcome. At Steam Age, none of the byproducts are obtainable, but this will become relevant soon.
{@pagebreak}
&lHow should I start?
The steps available in the Steam Age go as follows:
One Ore (block) &9->&r Two Crushed Ores (Macerator)
One Crushed Ore &9->&r One Impure Dust (Hammer)
One Impure Dust &9->&r One Dust (In world crafting)
One Dust &9->&r One Ingot (Furnace, you should know this one)
Beginner Ore Processing
First off, be sure to check the &9tooltip&r - there's a lot of information in there!
The bigger the Cleanroom, the longer it takes to become Clean.
&9Note&r: When the time comes, Multiblocks must also be put into Cleanrooms in order to run cleanroom recipes!
{@pagebreak}
Need to transfer EU? Try using &3Hulls&r or &3Diodes&r.
Item and Fluid transfer can be done using &3Passthrough Hatches&r.
&3Machine Hulls&r can also "double" as &6ME Cables&r to extend your ME Network inside your Cleanroom.
If you used any &dDoor(s)&r in the structure, they can remain open. Not very realistic, but convenient!
{@pagebreak}

&9&eConfigs:&r If you dislike the Cleanroom mechanics, it can be toggled off in the config file with &5"B:enableCleanroom"&r. Multiblocks can be made to ignore cleanroom requirements with &5"B:cleanMultiblocks"&r. We encourage you to try it out before deciding.
{@pagebreak}
Don't forget the &3Maintenance Hatch&r. If the structure refuses to form, rotate or replace the Controller, it can be a bit finicky. Don't worry - it doesn't have to be cube-shaped.

In the real world, a Cleanroom is a well-isolated room which maintains a very low concentration of dust and airborne particles. They're normally used for scientific research, and in real-life semiconductor manufacturing. Clean rooms are specifically designed to keep out as many airborne particulates as can be.
Clean rooms are also sometimes used with the purpose of preventing materials from escaping! This is often the primary aim in fields such as pharmaceutics, nuclear work, and hazardous biology.
The more you know!
The Controller always has to be in the center. The rest of the top layer has to be &dFilter Casings&r.
All edges have to be &dPlascrete&r, and the sides can be &dCleanroom Glass&r.
Placing &3Generators&r or &3Mufflers&r inside is &cnot allowed&r. They're too dirty, so the Cleanroom will unform.
{@pagebreak}
Upon assembly, the Cleanroom starts &4contaminated&r. While contamined, contained machines will not be able to operate.
The Cleanroom will drain 30 EU/t and slowly increase the cleanliness until its cleanliness is at 100%.
Once &9Clean&r, recipes can run. At that point it will only draw 4EU/t. Keep it powered at all times or it will get dirty again!
The Cleanroom
All About the Cleanroom
The &3Electric Blast Furnace&r requires a &3Muffler Hatch&r to run. This hatch must be &cunobstructed&r so it can output its beautiful smoke particles.
&l&3Lore:&r&o In GregTech 5, polluting multiblocks had Muffler Hatches. The higher tier the hatch, the lower the Pollution output.
&oPollution had... interesting... effects, such as turning grass and dirt into sand.
{@pagebreak}
When a recipe is performed, there is a small chance for the &3Muffler Hatch&r to give bonus items - typically tiny Dusts of Ash. These items can be processed for some helpful resources.
{@pagebreak}

Do &onot&r try to automate the extraction of items from the &3Muffler Hatch&r! It's not intended to be an automation challenge, as it voids excess contents when full, so don't worry about it stopping machines from running.
Muffler Hatches in GTCEu are more about pure aesthetic (c'mon, you can't deny that those particles look good!) and small rewards, rather than punishing game mechanics.
Muffler Hatches
&lWhy go parallel?
&9-&r &4Parallelization is superior&r to overclocking! Take advantage of this for your passive setups such as Ore Processing or Oil Distilling.
&9-&r &6Distinct buses&r: &3GCYM Machinery&r can accept multiple &3Input Buses&r. Use it for your pattern automation with &3Extruder&r, &3Engraver&r, and many other.
Power cost is based on the current recipe being run, times the number of &4parallel&r being performed.
Parallelisation
The quantity of 1 packet per tick is known as an Amp (1A for short).
Each single-block Generator in GregTech is configured to produce &91A&r of its voltage tier. For &7LV&r, that results in &232EU/t&r.
If a machine requires 16EU/t, one "packet" of 32EU is sent &6every other tick&r (assuming no cable loss) - no more, no less.
A Battery Buffer with &94&r Batteries can produce up to &94 Amps&r for &2128EU/t&r as &7LV&r power, which is important for the &3Electric Blast Furnace&r - or to run multiple machines simultaneously.
Generic machines are configured to draw up to &92 Amps&r to account for cable loss. Other machines have specific &9Amps IN&r, which is described in their tooltip.
{@pagebreak}
The most critical thing to know is that &acables&r have an &9Amperage &climit&r. Attempting to transport more Amps than this limit will &4burn your cable up&r.
&9Amps&r are drawn &oonly&r through the &aCables&r connecting the Producers and Consumers directly, and only drawn if the Consumers are active.
This means you can safely step down your Cables in certain places - feel free to experiment!
Amperage
There are many ways to automate Ordered Items: GT item pipes, Redstone, other mods, you name it! This quest will attempt to guide you through a setup using &3AE2&r.

Have the Pattern Provider face an &3Item P2P&r. Set two output P2Ps: one into the first &3Input Bus&r, and the other into &3Item Pipes&r. Make your Item Pipes connect to all Input Buses including the first. Don't forget &dBlocking Mode&r!
With this setup, assembly items should be fully automated!
{@pagebreak}
Whilst item automation was relatively simple, fluid automation is slightly harder.
Fluid Pipes behave differently compared to Item Pipes, so you &4won't&r be able to use the same solution as above.
This quest won't explain how to do this entirely &7(due to it being off by default)&r, so the full solution is left as an exercise to the reader.
Understanding the Assembly Line
&9-&r If the recipe isn't happening, check if the Multiblock is properly plugged in (we all make these mistakes!).
&9-&r Remember to always perform the initial Maintenance "routine" at the appropriate hatch.
&9-&r Verify the recipe's EU/t usage - the max EU/t provided to the multiblock has to be greater than that of the recipe.
{@pagebreak}
&9- &rCheck the special requirements the recipe may have (EMI always has some kind of indication if this is the case). Do you need to be in a Cleanroom, for example?
&9-&r Make sure the correct items are input into the buses/hatches. This is less obvious than in a regular machine, because you have to juggle between the Input Bus and Input Hatch.

&9-&r Make sure there is space for an output. Maybe the multiblock formed, but you forgot a Hatch. The other biggest offender is the Output Hatches being too low tier and thus having too little capacity - this trips people up with the Greenhouse!
It's not forming? We've all been there before.
Checkmark
Troubleshooting Multiblocks
Why does every machine have a million variants across each tier? We'll let you in on an industry secret - overclocking is one of the main reasons.
&9-&r &a4x&r power consumption
&9->&r &c2x&r total energy cost
As you can see, there are upsides and downsides. It is a game of balance: ask yourself if you want faster recipes at the cost of greater power consumption.

Overclocking is a mechanic that happens when you try to run a recipe in a machine &dthat is higher tier than the recipe itself.&r The recipe will use an increased amount of energy, but the recipe time will be cut based on how many tiers you're overclocking by.

&l&3Lore:&r&o GTCE overclocking was extremely awkward. If the recipe consumed 16EU/t or below, it would do a classic 2.0x overclock. However if the recipe consumed more than 16EU/t, every Overclock would be 2.8x faster! GTCEu has a config to select the Overclock speed bonus.
{@pagebreak}
A pro tip - for automated setups, overclock as little as possible!
Machines have a side menu to set the maximum voltage tier it will overclock to. Click on it to cycle through all the available Voltages and choose a limit.
{@pagebreak}
Each tier above the recipe tier allows one overclock. Each overclock implies:
&9-&r &a2x&r recipe speed
Overclocking

Simply put, Gregicality Multiblocks are larger versions of the GregTech machines you might be familiar with. The obvious increase in resource cost is worth your time, as they can be upgraded to gain the ability to process recipes in parallel.
{@pagebreak}

They also introduce Machine Modes - depending on the configured machine mode, the Multiblock will use a different recipe type when processing materials. You can change this from the machine GUI by clicking on the Robot Arm button.
{@pagebreak}

By including Parallel Control Hatches in your Gregicality Multiblocks, you can grant them parallel processing capability. There are 4 tiers of hatch, each further increasing parallel capability by an factor of 4.
{@pagebreak}

Batch mode can be enabled on a multiblock to merge together an amount of one recipe together into one recipe up to 5 seconds. This does not change the overall speed of one recipe like overclocking, but is useful to stop machine flickering.
This is not strictly gated by Gregicality Multiblocks, but is extremely useful with them.
Gregicality Multiblocks
Color by number multiblocks
Colored Buses
Colored Buses
Multiblocks do not look at the voltage of recipes when trying to craft. Instead, they simply check if they are being provided with enough Power.

&9Note:&r Be wary of Cable &closses&r bringing the actual power input below the recipe requirement! We &lhighly&r recommend either placing your &3Battery Buffer&r next to the &3Energy Hatches&r for the minimum cable length, or looking around this questbook to see if there are better alternatives to Cables.
{@pagebreak}

The EBF needs a minimum of &4120EU/t&r power input to run its recipes. This can be achieved with &3two LV Energy Hatches&r. Each one takes 2 Amps of LV, so that's 4 Amps of LV for 128EU/t maximum power.
Powering Multiblocks
You have likely realised by now that the Energy system in &2GregTech&r is &cnowhere near as simple&r as the &1RF&r you may be used to using in modded Minecraft.
The units are defined as such:
- &1EU&r is the unit of &1Energy&r.
- &9EU/t&r is the &9Power&r.
- &dA&r or &dAmp&r is the &dAmperage&r.
- &2V&r &owould&r be the &2Voltage&r, but we prefer referring to it as &7LV&r, &bMV&r, &6HV&r... as those are the relevant values for gameplay (technically: &7LV&r = 32V = 32EU/t/A).
{@pagebreak}
Electricity in GregTech travels in "packets". The size of each packet is equivalent to the voltage of its tier.
Taking an LV packet as an example, this "packet" would carry 32EU. Multiple blocks are capable of producing these EU packets, and packets are only produced if they are able to access a destination.
{@pagebreak}

Every &6tick&r, &1EU&r &apackets&r attempt to transfer themselves from Energy Producers to Consumers. These &apackets&r have two parameters: a &2Voltage&r tier determined by the tier of the Producer, and &dAmperage&r. This determines how much &9Power&r can actually be transferred.
The energy unit of GregTech is the EU.

There are no partial Amps, meaning Energy is transferred only if the full Amp &apacket&r can be received. You might notice this from your machines sitting just below full EU capacity - they will only accept EU when they are missing at least 1A of their input voltage.
{@pagebreak}
If a &3Machine&r receives a &2higher Voltage&r than its Tier, it'll &cexplode&r. Kaboom! Any excess &dAmperage&r won't have an adverse affect, as machines only consume as they need.
The machine explosion would usually also damage terrain, but we have disabled that feature in this pack.
{@pagebreak}

In summary, Energy is transported in &apackets&r of &132EU&r for &7LV&r, &1128EU&r for &bMV&r... so on and so forth. The amount of energy that is actually received by a machine can end up being lower than energy sent, due to cable loss.

Machine Energy Input is limited by &2Voltage&r (too high and, well, &6boom&r!), and by &dAmperage&r. Thus, a &bMV&r Machine with &d2A&r Input connected to a &7LV&r line will never accept more than &964EU/t&r.

It is still possible to run &bMV&r Machines on &7LV&r lines, but only if the recipes are low enough &9Power&r, or if you have a &3MV Battery&r in the charging slot. The machine will only accept &d1A&r when idle, and so the &3Battery&r will recharge at a maximum rate of &932EU/t&r.

&1EU&r mechanics have a certain flair to them, and are not dissimilar to real-world electricity. They can also be &4dangerous and punishing&r if mishandled. However, the power system gives GregTech players a lot of &6satisfaction&r when harnessed well.
&l&3Lore:&r&o The Amperage bug, exploit or feature (call it whatever you want!) from 1.12.2 GTCE has been &lfixed&r&o in GTCEu. The Energy network now works as intended.
{@pagebreak}
Let's go over some basic physics:
° &9Power&r = &2Voltage&r * &dAmperage&r
° &1Energy&r = &9Power&r * &6Time&r
&8Resistance&r is an excluded concept in GregTech, instead being partially simulated as cable loss.
Electricity
Maintenance in GregTech is not as bad as you think (promise!), and adding a Maintenance Hatch to your multiblocks makes them look pretty industrial!
{@pagebreak}
Most Multiblocks require a &3Maintenance Hatch&r. You will need to perform Maintenance for the Multiblock to begin operating.

This is done by having a &9Wrench&r, a &9Screwdriver&r, a &9Soft Mallet&r, a &9Hammer&r, a &9Wire Cutter&r, and a &9Crowbar&r in your inventory, opening the Maintenance Hatch and &eclicking the center spot once&r. &cThere's no need to move tools individually&r.
{@pagebreak}

Alternatively, you can circumvent these problems by placing a &9Tape&r in the Maintenance Hatch, but a lot of people would jump at the chance to tell you that Tape is &o"unethical"&r - plus, tape is gated behind some polymers starting from &bMV&r.
{@pagebreak}

Maintenance problems have a &d5%&r chance of occuring every &dhour of multiblock activity&r. Needless to say, they are &6very&r rare. Each maintenance problem increases the recipe duration by &c10%&r. Fixing these problems is done the same way as above.
At &6HV&r, you'll unlock other Maintenance Hatches that do not require manual repairs.
Maintenance Hatches
The &3Electric Blast Furnace&r, &3Pyrolyse Oven, &b&aMulti Smelter&r, and &3Cracking Unit&r all require Heating Coils. But why should you bother upgrading to higher tiers of Coil?
The Pyrolyse Oven is much more simple in comparison to the EBF.
Cupronickel coils apply a &c+25% penalty&r to recipe duration - effectively, recipes are slower than listed if one uses Cupronickel coils.
Kanthal coils restore recipe duration to a regular length of time.
However, coils above Kanthal apply an &aadditive -50% bonus&r to recipe duration!
{@pagebreak}
The Cracker is much more simple.
Every coil tier post-Cupronickel will reduce its energy usage by 10%.
Coils in the Multi Smelter reduce the amount of energy per operation whilst also increasing the number of items that can be processed in parallel.
Coil progression can be viewed in the Milestones tab.
{@pagebreak}

For the EBF, things get slightly complicated. The EBF smelts items at a certain &dtemperature&r. This is mainly determined by the tier of heating coil used - &r&6Cupronickel&r smelts at &d1800K&r, &bKanthal&r at &d2700K&r, etc. Additionally, starting from &6HV&r, each tier of energy adds &d100K&r to the temperature.
{@pagebreak}

How does this affect you? Each EBF recipe has a certain base temperature. For example, &bAluminium&r is smelted at &d1700K&r. If the EBF temperature is not high enough, the recipe won't happen. If the EBF temperature is high enough, 2 different bonuses are applied:
&9-&r For every &d900K&r above the recipe temperature, the amount of energy required is multiplied by &a0.95x&r - which stacks.
&9-&r For every &d1800K&r above the recipe temperature, a single additional overclock will be &6100% efficient&r; in other words, it will &5quadruple the recipe speed&r, instead of doubling it.
{@pagebreak}
Coil Behaviour

Scanning is the first step for research. Take the item shown in EMI and put it with a &3Data Stick&r to scan it. This will &4consume&r the item and put Data on the Data Stick. Pretty straightforward, right?
You will need at least an &6HV Scanner&r to progress to &dLuV&r, an &5EV Scanner&r for &aLuV Energy Hatches&r, and an &1IV Scanner&r for &aFusion Reactors&r.
{@pagebreak}

Later on, recipes will require different &aData Storage Items&r for research, such as the &3Data Orb&r. This process will remain the same, but will use different Data Storage Items instead. They can also be copied the same way, but you cannot copy between different types of storage items.
{@pagebreak}

Eventually, you'll want multiple Assembly Lines, but you won't want to re-scan for every Research. This is why you can also use the &3Scanner&r to &dCopy Data&r. Place the data stick you want to copy in one slot, and a blank one in the other. This will copy the contents of the first stick into the second!
&4Important&r: Using two different data sticks with data on them will cause one to &4overwrite&r the other. Be careful!
Implemented At Last
Research
You might already be familiar with EU as the Energy Unit for Electric machines - but what about Steam?
{@pagebreak}
Psst! If you're not in a Hardcore world, we invite you to stand on top of pipes transporting steam, or stand right in front of the vent as the machines are running recipes.
Steam machines will run using a proportional amount of steam at a 1:1 ratio of EU to Steam as listed in your recipe viewer of choice.
{@pagebreak}
After each recipe, the Steam machines will vent cooler steam (with snazzy particles) from the side with the square. This is the exhaust port.
Important: Keep the exhaust port unblocked - this is neither an input nor an output slot! If the machine fails to vent steam, it will stop working.
Reminder: Use your Wrench to change which side the exhaust port is facing (right-click).
{@pagebreak}
Regular Steam Machines are twice as slow to complete recipes as is listed in EMI. To bring your machines up to speed, you may want to pursue High Pressure Steam machinery.
High Pressure Steam Machines are the same speed as indicated by EMI, but with adjusted steam consumption. You will unlock them once you obtain Steel.
https://store.steampowered.com/
Steam Power
A shopping list for anyone looking to automate &6Ore Processing&r on a large scale:
What you may &ealso want to&r add:
&9-&r A few &3LV Ore Washers&r for quick washing purposes.
&9-&r Alternately, a &3Large Ore Washer&r, accompanied with a set of &3Distilleries&r for &dDistilled Water&r.
&9-&r A second &3Large Centrifuge&r... this time set to Centrifuge mode for impure/purified dusts.
&9-&r &3Chemical Baths&r for the special Byproducts that require &dMercury&r or &dSodium Persulfate&r to obtain.
&9-&r &3Sifters&r of any tier for gem ores.
&9-&r &3Electromagnetic Separators&r.
{@pagebreak}
If the Large Machines aren't your thing, you could always try using tons of &7LV&r machinery, and route with some clever piping.
Overclocking is &cnot&r energy efficient, which is why it is generally better to go for &6low-tier machines&r in &3passive setups&r. One could also argue they are cheaper.
&9-&r One or more &3IV Macerators&r.

In previous versions of GregTech, you could just use &3Processing Arrays&r, as they could condense many low-tier machines down into a &asingle speedy multiblock&r. Players desiring &esimilar processing speeds&r nowadays should really look to the &bGCYM machinery&r - it's quick, easy to upgrade when you tier up (&dEnergy Hatches&r are usually cheaper than 16 low-tier machines!), and c'mon now... they just look really cool.
{@pagebreak}
&o&7"Should I go for the optional byproducts?"
Yes.
However, the "routes" you take your ores through processing is up to you. Want to macerate twice because you prefer the other byproducts? Go ahead!
Note that &3Thermal Centrifuging&r is usually a good idea, as doing so unlocks a &6unique Byproduct&r from the maceration step.
{@pagebreak}
Chalcopyrite, Chalcocite, Bornite, Tetrahedrite, Pentlandite and Sheldonite ores should all be turned into their &dPurified Crushed&r variants and sent to your &6Platinum Group Metal&r chain.
Purified Crushed Galena/Sphalerite should be reserved for Indium until you set up the Naquadah line. At that point, you'll have more Indium than you'll ever need.
&aGallium&r, &aChrome&r, &aNiobium&r, &aRare Earths&r, and &aGlowstone&r are all &6Byproducts&r you might want to prioritise.
&9-&r The &3Large Centrifuge&r. Set it to work as a Thermal Centrifuge, and you're off to the races.
If you think we're missing any pertinent products, hit us up on Discord, and we'll be sure to add your favourites to this list.
{@pagebreak}
As you've probably realised, Applied Energistics 2 will be very, very helpful when automating all of this.

&3ME Storage Buses&r are very powerful for routing items when they enter your ME network. They also have a huge whitelist or blacklist configuration. Attach them to some &3Tungstensteel Crates&r to buffer intermediate items, or use a dedicated AE2 subnet.

To combine &aSmall Dusts&r into full &aDusts&r, you'll want a &3Storage Bus&r on high priority paired with an &dItem Tag&r filter set to &e&ldusts/small&r. Note that Small Dusts may be used for Boules, and a few Tiny Dusts are needed for the PBI chain, so you can blacklist them from the filter if you desire.
{@pagebreak}
For ores that you want to process quickly but don't care for the Byproducts as the full "route" would take too long in the machines, prioritize filtering them for quick washing.
The typically "best" path is: Macerator -> Ore Washing -> Thermal Centrifuge -> Macerator. If you deviate from it for various reasons, you're gonna have to set filters &emanually&r. Gasp!
&9-&r One or more &3MV Electrolyzers&r - you could possibly make the large version if there's enough demand.
&9-&r A &3Multi Smelter&r.
&9-&r A &3Packager&r of any tier for those pesky Small/Tiny Dusts (think Rare Earth!)
&9-&r Inventories acting as a large buffer, such as &3Tungstensteel Crates&r.
&9-&r &3ME Storage Buses&r, or a lot of &3Item Pipes&r + &aFilter covers&r, or &aItem Tag Filters&r.
{@pagebreak}

Ultimate Battery!
ftbquests.chapter.uv__ultimate_voltage.s: Bring your long journey to a well-deserved end
ftbquests.chapter.zpm__zero_point_module: &3Advanced HPCA Components&r are improved versions of their regular counterparts, and allow for increasing the computation you can produce from an HPCA.
The &3HPCA Advanced Computation Component&r produces &a4x&r the computation for only &a2x&r the Cooling!
Time for some computational advancement!
Advanced HPCA Components
The first Circuit of the &4Wetware&r line.
&6Congrats&r!
Eek, it's alive!
Best LuV Circuits!
The &3High Performance Computation Array&r, also known as the &3HPCA&r, is the multiblock used to create &9Computation&r, measured in CWU/t (Compute-Work Units per tick).
- &9Active Cooler&r: Requires power, PCB Coolant, but provides 2 cooling.
- &9Computation&r: Creates 4 CWU/t, but requires a lot of power and cooling.
{@pagebreak}
The HPCA draws some power to idle. Its power and cooling requirements will sit between the idle upkeep power and a maximum value depending on how much computation is being used.

If the HPCA is not given enough cooling, Computation components can be &4damaged&r if it is allowed to run above &c100C&r (the idle temperature is &a20C&r). Only computation components can be damaged - all other blocks will be unharmed!
The HPCA can only have 1 &3Computation Data Transmission Hatch&r. You can connect it to the Reception Hatch of the &9Research Station&r with Optical Fiber Cable to transmit the computation.
{@pagebreak}
Basic CWU/t Requirements for ZPM Tier:
- &a4 CWU/t&r for &cZPM&r Sensors, Emitters, and Field Generators
- &a8 CWU/t&r for &cZPM&r Enegy Hatches

The HPCA is a modular multiblock with many unique components you've likely not seen before. There are &a9 slots available&r for different components, and there are some example layouts in the EMI previews, so reviewing these may help if you feel confused.
- &a16 CWU/t&r for &3UV&r Circuits and beyond.
Don't feel forced to go for 16 CWU/t immediately. There's lots to do in between these milestones.
{@pagebreak}
&l&3Lore:&r&o This mechanic is loosely inspired by TecTech's Quantum Computer, which is similar but has some much more annoying mechanics like the Uncertainty Resolver.
{@pagebreak}
There are two main types of components:
- &9Computation Components&r: These generate CWU/t and require EU/t and cooling.
- &9Cooling Components&r: These provide a certain amount of cooling, and require EU/t.
Currently Available Components:
- &9Empty&r: Fills a slot but otherwise does nothing.
-&9 Heat Sink&r: Requires no power but provides 1 cooling.
That's no Quantum Computer...
HPCA
Build the structure displayed with Fusion Glass in &aEMI&r.
To save on Fusion Casings, fit Input + Output Hatches wherever you can (as displayed in the structure).
The &aFusion Reactor Mk2&r is even more expensive than the Mk1! The key difference is that it has a higher &6Energy To Start&r than the Mk1, allowing you to run new recipes.
It can also overclock lower voltage recipes, such as those in the Mk1 reactor. See the Mk1's quest for how these mechanics work.
Fusion just got more expensive...
Fusion Reactor II
&aZPM Superconductors&r are a major gate between you and a &9Fusion Reactor Mk2&r, which uses copious amounts for its structure blocks.
You can also use them to make &9Superconducting Coils&r for cheaper.
Getting tired of all these pitch-black ingots yet?
ZPM Superconductors
The &aCrystal SoC&r is used to make cheaper &9Crystal Circuits&r. Enjoy the discount!
Crystal SoCs require &9ZPM Emitters&r, which means you need a &9Data Orb&r for their research.
In the future, these may become more difficult to make.
{@pagebreak}

&l&3Lore:&r&o In GT5u, the texture for this item was red, and did not have the special design on it. There was a "raw" version with the design, but it was used for other unrelated things. Who knows why?
When engraving it once isn't enough
Crystal SoC
&aDuranium&r is a material from Star Trek, and is used for a few things in GT. It makes some pretty awesome pipes, but otherwise you won't need much of this quite yet.
{@pagebreak}
&l&3Lore:&r&o In some versions of GT5u, this material was entirely white. In fact, most fusion materials and later were like this. Boring!
Who needs Stargate, anyway?
Duranium
This texture used to be really ugly...
Stem Cells
The third circuit of the &4wetware&r line. Get some &bEuropium&r to make these.
This is also the best &3UV&r circuit!
Sentience in circuit form
Best UV Circuits!
&aTritanium&r is a material from Star Trek, and is used for a few other things in GT. It, like &9Americium&r, requires two fusion steps!
You'll need this to get the next tier of circuits, and for &3UV&r components.
{@pagebreak}
&l&3Lore:&r&o In some versions of GT5u, only Tritanium fluid was red. The material was otherwise white. In GTCEu, we decided to make the whole thing red instead. Much better looking!
Star Trek strikes again!
Tritanium
The second circuit of the &4wetware&r line.
This is also the best &cZPM&r circuit!
Did that circuit just BLINK at me?
Best ZPM Circuits!
Neurons for computation
It's Alive!
The &3Research Station&r is the upgrade to the Scanner. It's used for more advanced forms of research, and will finally allow you to perform research which requires &aData Orbs and Modules&r.

When running the &3Research Station&r, energy and &9Computation&r is needed. The latter is provided through an &9HPCA&r, which is explained in the next quest. It is recieved with a &3Computation Data Reception Hatch&r. Note that only one Reception Hatch is allowed in a Research Station.
{@pagebreak}

This multiblock needs computation &dsporadically&r, which means the recipe will not reverse progress if you don't supply enough - it will simply halt in-place. However, the machine will still draw energy constantly, even when recieving no computation.

To scan items, the process is relatively similar. In the &3Object Holder&r, place the target item in the center slot, and the data storage item in the other slot. Then provide computation, and the data storage item will be updated upon completion. When running, the target item will be Locked and cannot be removed.
&eNote&r: To form this multiblock, the &3Object Holder&r must face the controller.
Your research adventures continue!
Research Station
&aTrinium Coils&r bring up the Heat Capacity to &d9,001K&r.
These coils are required for progressing to the second half of &cZPM&r, and beyond.
IT'S OVER 9000!!!
Trinium Coils
&cZPM&r Components thankfully aren't too much harder than &dLuV&r.
They use lots of &9Osmiridium&r, so make sure your platinum refining process is up to the task.
Prepare your platline!
Absolute Elation
This Quest will be completed with &eeither&r a &3ZPM Energy Hatch&r&r... or a &3ZPM Dynamo Hatch&r for your Multiblock Generators.
Don't forget that &d16 Amp&r variants exist!
Don't forget that these hatches require a &9Data Orb&r for research.
Upgrading your Assembly Line II
The final circuit board - it's been a long time coming! As you can see, this board is &cmuch&r more expensive than the other ones, but you should be alright. You're a pro now!
{@pagebreak}
&l&3Lore:&r&o In GTNH, these circuit boards require LuV Sensors, instead of IV. This means that Wetware LuV circuits, needed other (crystal) LuV circuits!

Additionally, because Wetware was so expensive, using Crystal was preferred unless UHV wetware circuits were needed. Thankfully, CEu does not have this problem, and LuV Wetware Circuits are worth making.
The board of life itself
Wetware Printed Circuit Board
The &aZPM Lapotronic Orb&r is even better than the &dLuV&r one! It of course comes at a price...
{@pagebreak}
&l&3Lore:&r&o Imagine making 64 &1IV&f or 8 &dLuV&f Orbs for just one of these! See the Lore for the &dLuV&f orb for details.
A power singularity!
Mega Batteries
The &aSterilized Cleanroom&r is required to produce the next tier of circuits. Nearly every step must be performed inside of one. Good luck fitting everything into such a tight space!
If you only have one &3Cleanroom&r, you'll need another for &aSterilized&r recipes.
&eNote&r: Normal Cleanroom recipes cannot run in the Sterilized Cleanroom, so you can't just "upgrade" your old Cleanrooms.
Comes with disinfectant!
Sterilized Cleanroom
Remember &aDarmstadtium&r tools from &3GTCE&r? Well then... guess who's back?
&aDarmstadtium&r is the main material for &3UV&r hulls. It is yet again made with Fusion.
{@pagebreak}
&bFun Fact&r: Arsenic does not exist as a liquid at standard conditions. It sublimates directly into a gas! "Realism", my ass.
I want my particle accelerator back...
Darmstadtium
Production of &aSterilized Growth Medium&r is the final processing line in GTCEu, for now.
{@pagebreak}
&l&3Even More Lore:&r&o In Shadows of Greg, this was made with just Distilled Water and Mince Meat. How far we've come...
You will need this for your first &4Wetware Circuits&r.
Producing it won't be as much of a hassle as PBI, but nearly every step requires a Sterilized Cleanroom. This means you'll have to get creative with how you use your space.
Make sure to scrutinise every step of the chain. Some recipes are much more efficient than others!
&ePro Tip&r: You can wall-share cleanrooms with doors in-between too if you want more space.
{@pagebreak}

&l&3Lore:&r&o GTCEu's Sterilized Growth Medium chain is loosely based off of Bartworks' from GTNH. The main difference is that GTNH required a Bacterial Vat multiblock, which was more complex than the ordered Assembly Line. GTCEu is considering adding a multiblock like it but with their own spin in the future.
{@pagebreak}

&l&3More Lore:&r&o In Gregicality Legacy, the Sterilized Growth Medium production chain was very different. It was one of the most difficult processes in the mod, with over 30 complicated steps! It was based off of producing different real-life vitamins and nutrients.
The final processing line, at last!
Sterilized Growth Medium
Naquadah, but radioactive-er!
Naquadria
This hatch allows you to store more &aData Storage Items&r than the basic one.
Don't forget that this hatch requires a &9Data Orb&r for research.
Increased storage density!
Advanced Data Access Hatch
&aEnriched Naquadah&r is an isotope of Naquadah, Nq-528. It is radioactive and will be used in (as of yet) unimplemented nuclear reactors.
Currently, you just need it to make &9Trinium Coils&r.
Naquadah, but radioactive!
Enriched Naquadah
The &aZero Point Module&r (item) is a non-rechargable battery with TONS of energy stored. You may have found one of these before now, but you haven't been able to discharge it until reaching &cZPM&r.
These can only be found as loot from &6Jungle Temples&r. They're exceptionally rare - don't worry about finding one.
This quest is &6optional&r and is just for fun. Feel free to hit the checkbox if you just want the completion points!
{@pagebreak}
&l&3Lore:&r&o Zero Point Module, the full name of the ZPM tier, is also from Stargate. Its namesake is a device which generated crazy amounts of energy.
Unlimited powah!
Zero Point Module
&aAmericium&r is a Fusion Mk2 material, used in large quantities in CEu progression!
It requires 2 Fusion steps to obtain - Lanthanum and Silicon will make &bLutetium&r, and combining this &bLutetium&r with Chrome will give you &aAmericium&r.
{@pagebreak}
&l&3Lore:&r&o In Gregicality Legacy, Americium was replaced with Dubnium. Americium is a material only obtained from nuclear reactors, so GCYL changed it to the synthetic element Dubnium instead.
It'd be nice if we could make this in a nuclear reactor...
Americium
The &aUV Mainframe&r is required to move into &3Fusion Mk2&r.
It's also made in the Assembly Line.
Passing over the ingredients we've already seen before, watch out for the &6HSS-E Frames&r.
...ah, here we go!
First UV Circuits!
Harness the cosmos and wield the bacteriological
&cZPM&r - Zero Point Module
ftbquests.chapter.fish_tank.quest469CEB4: Completeting the Fish Tank gives you the &3Neptunium-Infused Hook&r. This can be added to your rod to give you higher luck and a chance to catch &6Relic Troves&r.
ftbquests.chapter.fish_tank.title: Fish Tank
ftbquests.chapter.fishing.title: Fish
ftbquests.chapter.gems.title: Gems
ftbquests.chapter.getting_started.quest1: Gather logs and stone, and submit them to this quest in order to receive a free starter farmhouse.
You can see a preview of these by talking to Ace the Carpenter and selecting 'Build Farm Buildings'.
Upgrading your tools past wood requires a &6Smithing Table&r. At higher tiers it will require a Smithing Template purchased from a &6Blacksmith Villager&r.
Tools can be repaired in an anvil infinitely, and enchantments also carry over when upgrading!
Search for an item in the item list sidebar and &6Left Click&r on it to see its recipes.
You can share a bank account with your friends in multiplayer!
Purchase a &6Blaze Banker&r and a &6White ID Card&r + &6White Card&r for each player from the &6Banker&r villager. Each player must right click to bind the ID card and add it to the Blaze Banker.
Finally, place &6White Card&r into the bottom left slot of the Blaze Banker to bind it. You can then access the account by right clicking a &6Bank Terminal&r with the card.
Placing the White Card in your curio slot will allow you to purchase items from villagers using shared funds.
ftbquests.chapter.getting_started.quest2: Can't be bothered to run up to every villager every time you need something??
The &6Phone&r has you covered! Right clicking on it will allow you to select which villager to trade with over the phone. Some shops can only be accessed over the phone!
It is sold by the &6Banker&r Villager.
Your farm isn't going to be very successful if you stick to those &6Stone Tools&r...
The &6Carpenter&r can help you build a home for a &6Blacksmith&r. They'll sell you smithing templates to upgrade your tools to iron.
Wondering why your tools aren't breaking? All of the main tools and armors have &6infinite&r durability when used.
There's one small tradeoff: these tools lose 15%% + 15 durability on death. This only applies to equipment in your hotbar and armor.
Tools can be repaired in an anvil infinitely, with significantly lower experience costs. Unbreaking also reduces the amount of durability lost.
You may notice the tiers of armor and tools have been slightly tweaked.
Iron now upgrades to &6Gold&r before &bDiamond&r, adding another step in progression.
Unlike vanilla, the &6Gold&r tools are balanced inbetween both tiers.
ftbquests.chapter.getting_started.quest3: &6There's no rush in placing villager building blueprints!&r
It can be a ton of work to terraform while trying to build your farm. These blueprints are optional and can always be placed later when you're more established.
You can always move the &6Villager Home&r block after placing it.
Not enough space...
Understood!
So many Blueprints!
&6Prize Tickets&r can be found as a reward from some harder bounties.
Each time you submit one to a &6Prize Machine&r, you'll receive an item. The more you submit, the better the rewards are until it loops.
Right click on the &6Prize Machine&r for a hint on the next prize!
Cool Prizes
The &6Bounty Board&r will have bounties requesting different items or tasks done in exchange for coins or other items.
Right click a completed bounty on the board to complete.
By default it will come with one of four different types of &6Decrees&r, which determine which items will be requested.
Bounties
&6Blueprints&r can be used to instantly build pre-made buildings, without the need to collect every block!
&6Right Click&r a block with a blueprint to place a preview. Right click again to open the menu.
&6Ctrl + Scroll Wheel&r can be used to nudge the blueprint in the direction you scroll.
The menu can be used to rotate, mirror, and &6build&r!
Any Blueprint
Placing Blueprints
This questline will take you through the basics of the pack to get you started farming.
The Basics
Strengthening your bond with the villagers will make them feel more at home in your town!
&6Shift + Right Click&r on a villager to give them a gift once every 4 days.
Things that have a sell value are always giftable, but you can find the full list by searching &6#villager_gift&r in JEI/EMI.
Understood!
Giving Gifts
To get started making money, you'll need a &6Basic Shipping Bin&r.
Items placed inside that have a sell value will be sold at &66 AM&r for the value listed in the tooltip.
Making Money
ftbquests.chapter.getting_started.quest4: There are 5 skill trees that can be leveled, unlocking special abilities useful to you. You can view these trees using &6K&r by default.
&6Farming&r experience comes from harvesting crops, eating cooked meals, and using Artisan Machines (such as Preserves Jars or Looms).
&6Husbandry&r experience comes from taking care of animals.
&6Mining&r experience comes from mining ores and Geode Nodes, provided you aren't using Silk Touch.
&6Fishing&r experience comes from catching fish, crafting fishing equipment, and harvesting from Fish Ponds.
&6Adventuring&r experience comes from killing mobs and especially from looting chests.
Unlike vanilla Minecraft, crops need water to grow, and farmland won't be hydrated from nearby water!
They can be watered using a &6Watering Can&r, which will need to be done every day.
Every morning at &66 AM&r, farmland will dry up and crops will grow on your farm. If the farmland is dry, your crops will die!
The &6Banker&r can provide you with tools that make managing your money significantly easier.
You'll need to invite a &6Market&r villager to purchase this invitation.
ftbquests.chapter.getting_started.quest6: Building a successful farm is not something you can do alone! Crafting the &6Carpenter Invitation&r is your next step!
The &6Carpenter&r can get you started, helping you build homes for new villagers and offering building supplies if you want to make them yourself.
You can preview what all the different villager buildings given as quest rewards look like by talking to the Carpenter.
By now you've probably become annoyed with storing the many items on your journey.
A &6Backpack&r will come in handy, purchase one from the &6Market&r villager.
Skill paths split multiple times, and you might not like what you've picked!
Thankfully the &6Witch&r villager sells &6Crystals of Regret&r for each skill tree. They are one-time use, resetting your skill tree completely.
It refunds &65 skill points&r, so you don't have to start completely from 0.
ftbquests.chapter.getting_started.quest7: There are 6 main tiers of &6Coins&r, and they can be crafted up or down from the previous tier.

Hoarding your coins in random chests isn't ideal. The &6Bank Terminal&r is an ATM, allowing you to store your coins safely. You can access your money from any other Bank Terminal, like an Ender Chest.
It can be purchased from the &6Banker&r villager.
Some biomes such as &6Savannas&r and &6Jungles&r will always be treated as &6Summer&r for crop growth only. They will be marked as "Wet Season" and "Dry Season".
This can be used to create a secondary farm that has no need to worry about seasons!
The same applies to frozen biomes for &6Winter&r.
ftbquests.chapter.getting_started.title: I - Getting Started
ftbquests.chapter.ii__building_up_the_fa: Cooking is essential early on, for both keeping you alive in the mines and making profit.
A few basic ones can be crafted using &6Earth Crystals&r.
In general, cooked meals are worth &61.2x-2x the sum of their ingredients&r! Complex dishes (ones with many ingredients) have an additional boost to their value as well.
Any cooking station
Getting Cooking
&6Preserve Jars&r turn fruits and vegetables into preserves in &64&r days, multiplying their selling value by over &63&r.
Having many run in the background is worth the investment.
Any compostable material can be used on a &6Worm Farm&r to produce worms.
A much cheaper alternative to purchasing them.
Turning Eggs into Mayonnaise is a good way of increasing profits from chickens.
This can be done with a &6Mayonnaise Machine&r in &61&r day.
&oYou'll want to take a look at the farming quest line for information on how to get the ingredients for one.&r
Brewing beer is a good way to start on producing &6Artisan Goods&r on your farm.
Dried ingredients need to be processed in the &6Silo&r.
The Brewing process itself requires attention and is slightly complex. You can hold &6W&r while hovering over the Brewingstation to learn how to brew beer.
Brewing Beer
&6Fertilizer&r is a huge step in upgrading how much your farm produces.
Simply right click on the farmland to gain the affects.
Any Fertilizer
All on Fertilizers
The next place to exploit for its resources is the &6Nether&r.
It's a dangerous place, but has the important resource &6Fire Quartz&r, needed for advanced farm building.
Getting to the Nether
The &6Sewing Table&r can cut Artisan Canvas into clothing and hats when combined with other materials.
It requires a &6Sewing Needle&r to craft.
Crafting it with a &6Chest&r allows it to retain its inventory.
Sewing Clothing
Tired of paying the Blacksmith to open &6Geodes&r? Buy the &6Extractinator&r from one!
Right click it with a &6Geode&r to pop it open, free of charge.
Free Geode Busting
Upgraded rods can be equipped with attachments using a &6Tackle Box&r.
They will also have a chance to upgrade enchantments from succesful catches. The chance increases on higher upgraded rods.
Higher tiers of rods will also increase the size of the minigame bobber!
Any upgraded fishing rod
Upgrading Your Rod
&6Pine Tar&r is tapped from Spruce and Pine trees and is mainly used for advanced farming devices.
&6Deluxe Crab Trap Bait&r improves the chance of catching seafood and treasure from Crab traps, and decreases the chance of junk.
The Deluxe Worm Bin upgrades basic &6Crab Trap Bait&r in &61&r day.
Mining ores in cold biomes or &bWinter&r will have a chance to give you &6Frozen Geodes&r.
Outside of that they can drop from &6Slush&r in cold biomes (affected by fortune), or frozen zombies in &bWinter&r.
The fish you'll catch depends on 4 factors: &aSeason&r, &6Location&r &aWeather&r, and &6Time&r.
Each of the four &aseasons&r have their own fish. Each &6location&r (Ocean, River, or Freshwater) has its own pool.
Finally, some fish can only be caught during night or day.
Baits can be added using a &6Tackle Box&r and decrease the amount of time between bites.
They are slowly consumed, and better baits such as &6Leeches&r and &6Minnows&r have a higher amount of durability.
Any Bait
Baiting Fish
Figuring out which Fish can be caught in a given location can be tricky. Some have very specific spawning conditions on top of being very rare.
The &6Fish Finder&r lists out every fish in the game and its exact spawn conditions. It can either be found or purchased from a &6Fisher&r.
Fishing Guide
Oak, Dark Oak, Spruce, and Pine trees can be tapped using a &6Tapper&r.
The type of tree tapped will determine how many days it will take to complete as well as the output.
Tapping Wood
All farm animals require &6Animal Feed&r regularly to produce their products. They need to be fed once every Minecraft day.
If an animal goes too long without being fed, they won't be very happy with you...
Feeding Animals
Raising Animals
Each sellable item in the pack has one of four categories:
- 🔱 &6Farmer&r - Raw crops and cooked meals
- ✎ &6Artisan&r - Items made in Artisan Machines by hand, such as Preserves, Beer, Wine, Cheese, etc.
- 🎣 &6Geologist&r - Ores, gems, and minerals. Anything out of the ground.
- 🗡 &6Adventurer&r - Looted artifacts and other rare items.
The category is only relevant when it comes to skills, which may increase certain categories if taken.
Understood!
Artisan Goods?
&6Truffles&r are valuable goods, found by Pigs when they have at least 5 hearts of affection.
&6Geode Nodes&r rarely found in caves have a chance of dropping &6Aquamarine,&r the main crafting material for fishing related tools.
Farm animals require love and attention! They can be pet once a day with an added bonus if you feed them by hand.
Cramped conditions where more than 6 or so animals are walled in or packed together will make them lose happiness.
Right click a farm animal with an empty hand to see their affection.
Understood
Affection
Baits can be added using a &6Tackle Box&r and have various effects on your rod.
Any fishing hook
Fishing Hooks
Animals are sensitive to changes in their care or environment. They may really like you, but if you mistreat them it'll effect their produce!
You can check how an animal is feeling by right clicking them with an empty hand.
- Smiles (☺) indicate the animal is happy! They'll produce quality items.
- Frowns (☹) indicate the animal is sad, giving them a chance to not produce that day.
You can get detailed information on an animal's mood by right clicking them with the &6Mood Scanner&r purchased from the Shepherd.
Animal Mood
Fish are a fast and valuable way to make money early game.
Your first rod will come from the &6Fisher&r villager, and they otherwise sell aquatic and fishing related supplies.
Welcoming Haruna
Invited the Fisher villager
Fishing
By now your storage situation may be getting dire. Thankfully the &6Librarian&r villager sells tools for sorting your base out.
At the end of every season, you'll also have access to the &6Book fair&r, a special shop that sells different skill books.
Welcoming Veronica
Invited the Librarian
&6Small Ships&r can be crafted using &6Artisan Canvas&r, allowing quicker sailing through the ocean. By default, the &6R&r hotkey can be used to drop the sail.
These can be used to transport large amounts of exotic farm animals from far away lands.
Set Sail
Birds such as Chickens will produce eggs, but won't produce them as fast when at lower levels of affection.
They'll produce larger eggs at high levels of affection.
Any egg
Eggs
&3Neptunium&r is a precious material used in crafting advanced fishing gear.
It can be found in &3Neptune's Bounty&r you fish up, or rarely in Crab Traps.
Beds can keep you stuck in one place to avoid losing your home.
The &6Sleeping Bag&r solves this by allowing you to sleep away the night while not setting your spawn.
Sleep Anywhere
Watering your crops every morning gets old fast.
&6Sprinklers&r help you out by keeping farmland hydrated in a radius around them.
The basic Iron tier works in a 3x3 area centered around it.
They can also be right clicked with a stick to add support for decoration.
The &6Wireless Crafting Grid&r allows you to access your storage network from a distance!
You'll also need to purchase a &6Wireless Transmitter&r and place it somewhere on your network. Multiple can be added at different areas of your base to cover a wider area!
Alternatively, their range can be extended with &6Range Upgrades&r.
Wireless Access
&6Treated Logs&r can be made by right clicking Oak Resin onto any Log in world.
Buying seeds for crops that require them really eats into your margins. The &6Seed Maker&r turns crops into seeds for free.
Using crops with any quality will turn the seed into the lowest quality inputed into the &6Seed Maker&r in &61&r day.
Quality seeds will have a higher chance to grow quality crops, making it worth your time to produce good seeds!
The fishing minigame can be turned on and off at any time using the command:
&6/stardew_fishing toggle_minigame&r
You won't be able to catch quality fish or get extra treasure, but those can both be obtained using other methods!
Understood!
Don't like the minigame?
The &6Farmer's Almanac&r has detailed information of crops and farm animals, which is essential when deciding what to focus on every season.
It is sold by the &6Market&r and &6Shepherd&r
All on Farming
The &6Canvas Loom&r is an artisan machine for making &6Artisan Canvas&r and &6Merino Wool&r in &61&r day.
These products can either be sold, crafted into useful items, or sewn into clothing using a &6Sewing Table&r.
Cows, Sheep, Goats, Wooly Cows, and Water Buffalos can all be milked.
Milking animals requires a special &6Milk Pail&r for collection.
The size of the milk will depend on how much the animal likes you!
Any milk
Milk
Bundles are the first large goal of the pack. They require certain items to be submitted, giving small rewards for each bundle, and large rewards when all bundles are completed.
The most important right now is:
Consisting of products that can grow on your farm.
The Spring Crops Bundle (Click Me)
Bundles

&6Enriched Bonemeal&r can be used to grow crops such as Glowberries, Lavender, and Hibiscus.

Tasty Luring
High quality items can lead to a huge increase in profits, but it can make automation and storage a hassle.

Not all mushrooms can be cultivated on &6Mushroom Soil&r. The power of the &6Mossberry&r can be used to make the &6Mushroom Log&r!

Mining ore in the Skull Cavern has a chance to drop &6Omni Geodes&r.

&6Refined Storage systems&r aren't great at handling many different types of non-stacking items!

I won't do that!

The &6Guild&r will now sell you &6Collar Tags&r, a conduit for enchanting your pets to make them battle-ready.
Powerful Beasts

The &6Statue of The Moon Gnome&r channels the ancient power of Selene. It can be crafted by a &6Blacksmith&r using Iridium Ingots.

Reach level 12 in every skill
Unlock Skill Mastery
Skill Mastery
The &6Auto-Petter&r is a rare drop from &6Grimwood Supply Crates&r in the Blackstone Caves.
It is a machine filled with ancient power that pets nearby animals every morning, steadily increasing their affection when you're not around. They love it!
The fourth and final layer of the Skull Cavern is made up of the Umbra Barrens and Blackstone Caves.

&6Networked Pipes&r are capable of complex logistical operations. They can be used to sort, auto-stock, auto craft, and auto-retrieve items from pipe networks.

Quality Pickling
Unlocking &6Husbandry Mastery&r allows you to upgrade the production of your animals significantly.
Unlock Husbandry Mastery
Unlocking &6Mining Mastery&r will provide mining riches past your wildest dreams!

Unlock Mining Mastery
